summaries.summary: A ChatGPT workspace is how OpenAI delivers ChatGPT Enterprise, Business and Edu access. Built-in roles are Owner (workspace-wide settings), Admin (supported operations and groups), Member (no admin rights) and Analytics Viewer, and a ChatGPT or Codex seat type decides which product surfaces a member can use. Groups can be manual, IdP-managed through SCIM, or dynamic; for SCIM-managed members, remove access in the IdP because a later sync can restore it.

The Claude Admin API is Anthropic's programmatic interface for managing workspaces, API keys, rate limits and members, exposed in the SDKs under client.organization (GA since 2026-09-30). It is available to Claude Console and Claude Enterprise organizations, not Team plans or individual accounts. It accepts Admin API keys, non-workspace-scoped personal or service account keys, or org:admin OAuth tokens. It cannot create API keys, only list, rename or change their status, and it can assign only the user and managed roles.

The Claude Agent SDK is Anthropic's agent framework (Python claude-agent-sdk 0.2.182, TypeScript @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.325), renamed from the Claude Code SDK. It runs the bundled Claude Code binary and exposes query() and ClaudeAgentOptions with built-in tools, hooks, subagents, MCP, permissions, sessions, skills and plugins, using a minimal system prompt unless the claude_code preset is requested. Third-party products must authenticate with API keys or Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or Claude Platform on AWS, not claude.ai login.

claude.ai is Anthropic's chat product and the management console for Claude Team and Enterprise organizations, separate from Claude Console organizations, so a company using both creates admin keys in each. Its Admin role does not include the Plugins & skills page, and exact Team role names are unconfirmed. Remote MCP servers such as Google Cloud MCP connect as custom connectors using an OAuth client registered with the claude.ai MCP auth callback as redirect URI.

The Claude API is Anthropic's REST API at api.anthropic.com (Messages, Batches, token counting, Models, Files, Skills), streaming via SSE and billed per million tokens. Requests authenticate with an API key or WIF token, send anthropic-version (current 2026-10-21, which removes temperature, top_p and top_k), and need anthropic-workspace-id for non-workspace-scoped keys. Opus, Sonnet and Haiku 5.5 get 4,000 to 13,000 RPM by tier; 429 signals rate, ramp or spend limits. There is no hosted vector store or PrivateLink.

A Claude API key is Anthropic's static credential (sk-ant-api...) sent as Authorization: Bearer or legacy x-api-key. Personal and service account keys can be scoped to one workspace or all accessible workspaces; unscoped keys must send anthropic-workspace-id or get 400. Since 2026-07-08 expiration is fixed at creation (3 hours to Never, with an org maximum policy able to remove Never), and expired keys return 401 and cannot be reactivated. Agent SDK third-party products must use API keys rather than claude.ai login.

Claude API usage tiers are Anthropic's spend and rate-limit levels, consolidated on 2026-06-26 into Start ($500 monthly cap), Build ($1,000), Scale ($200,000) and uncapped Custom, with new organizations possibly starting in a lower Evaluation tier. Hitting the tier spend cap returns 429 rate_limit_error with error_code enforced_spend_limit_reached and no retry-after, so retries fail until the next month.

Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding CLI (2.1.325, released 2026-11-13), also bundled by the Agent SDK. It authenticates via Pro/Max/Ultra/Team/Enterprise accounts, Console (keyless since 2.1.242), Bedrock, Google Cloud, Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS, gateways or WIF; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY outranks subscription login. Admins can force login method and allowed providers through managed settings. Console sign-in creates a separate Claude Code workspace with per-user keys and spend limits. It supports MCP servers, 33 hook events and headless claude -p.

The Claude code execution tool is Anthropic's stable server-side sandbox (versions code_execution_20250825, 20260120 and 20260521), required for Agent Skills and enabling programmatic tool calling. Containers have 5 GiB RAM, 5 GiB disk, 1 CPU, no internet, and expire 30 days after creation. Each organization gets 1,550 free hours per month, then $0.05 per container-hour, and it is free when used with newer web search or web fetch versions.

Claude Code GitHub Actions (anthropics/claude-code-action@v1) is Anthropic's action that responds to @claude mentions or runs a prompt in GitHub workflows. It authenticates with an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret, or keylessly via GitHub OIDC with anthropic_federation_rule_id, and supports Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry via OIDC. Commits with the default GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger CI, triggering users need write access, bots need allowed_bots, and @beta workflows must move to @v1.

The Claude Compliance API is Anthropic's Enterprise audit and content-export interface under /v1/compliance/*, adding over Claude for Teams. Its Activity Feed (retained 6 years) works with Console Admin API keys or Enterprise keys holding read:compliance_activities, while content endpoints (chats, files, projects, Claude Code and Cowork transcripts) and directory endpoints require an Enterprise Compliance Access Key. It shares a 600 requests per minute limit per parent organization.

Claude Console is Anthropic's developer console where Console organizations hold API workloads, separate from claude.ai Enterprise tenancy. Its hierarchy is organization then workspaces (wrkspc_ IDs) holding members, service accounts, API keys and limits. The support article lists six roles: User, Claude Code User, Limited Developer, Developer, Billing and Admin. MFA enforcement is undocumented and delegated to the customer IdP under required SSO. It includes a Managed Agents session viewer.

The Claude Console admin role is Anthropic's organization-level administrator, holding all other role permissions plus user management; owners and primary owners add the ability to manage admins. Only admins create workspaces, service accounts, federation issuers and rules, Admin API keys and IP allowlists, and set up WIF. Admins automatically become Workspace Admin in every workspace, while users and developers must be added explicitly, so agent builders typically need an admin to provision their runtime identity.

A Claude Console workspace (wrkspc_ ID) is Anthropic's unit for grouping members, service accounts, API keys and limits under an organization, created by org admins in the Console or via the Admin API. The default cap is 100 workspaces per organization. Files, batches, Skills and prompt caches are isolated per workspace on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Foundry. Per-model RPM, ITPM and OTPM limits can be set below org limits.

The Claude Consumption Unit (CCU) is Anthropic's billing unit for Claude Platform on AWS and Claude in Microsoft Foundry. Usage is rated at standard per-model rates, discounted, converted at $0.01 per CCU, metered hourly to AWS Marketplace or Azure Marketplace, and invoiced monthly in arrears with no prepaid credits, which matters when budgeting agent workloads through cloud marketplaces.

Claude custom connectors let Anthropic's Claude apps add remote MCP servers by URL, on Free (one connector) through Enterprise plans. On Team and Enterprise an Owner adds them in Organization settings and members connect individually; connections originate from Anthropic's cloud, not the user's device. Auth options are Claude's published identity (recommended), Dynamic Client Registration, your own OAuth client, or beta static headers. URLs ending /sse use the older transport, and auth settings cannot be edited after adding.

Claude Enterprise is Anthropic's sales-led plan whose tenant has one parent organization centralizing identity, linking claude.ai organizations and Claude Console organizations. Over Team it adds domain capture, role-based permissions, the Compliance API and inference hooks; roles are user, managed, owner, membership_admin and primary_owner. Qualified accounts can get a separate Claude Code ZDR offering. As shown 2026-11-14 it cost $20 per seat monthly billed annually, 20-seat minimum, plus usage at API rates.

A Claude Enterprise Admin API key is Anthropic's scoped admin credential created in claude.ai Organization settings with prefix sk-ant-api01-. Scopes cover members, RBAC groups, plugins, Claude tag, spend limits, analytics, compliance activities and data, and org audit. The primary owner can grant any scope, while owners can grant only Compliance scopes. The Spend Limits API requires read or write spend_limits scopes.

Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2) is one of Anthropic's latest models, with a 1M-token context window, 128K max output and a June 2026 training cutoff, priced at $8 input and $40 output per MTok as shown 2026-11-14. Rate limits run from 4,000 RPM (Start) to 13,000 RPM (Scale). It reached GA in Google Model Garden on 2026-11-09 with fast mode, and retires no sooner than 2027-11-09.

Claude fast mode is Anthropic's premium speed tier (speed: "fast") delivering up to 2.5x output tokens per second with dedicated rate limits. It defaults on Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.2 and Opus 5.5, is a research preview on Opus 5, and is deprecated on Opus 4.8 with removal on 2026-11-30. Prices as shown 2026-11-14 are $16/$80 for Fable and Mythos 5.2 and $8/$40 for Opus 5.5 per MTok. It is unavailable with the Batch API.

The Claude Files API is Anthropic's file upload service at /v1/files, GA since 2026-08-19 with no beta header. It accepts files up to 500 MB, 1 TB per organization, about 500 requests per minute, with optional expiry. Uploaded files are not downloadable; only skill and code-execution outputs are. Files and Skills are workspace-scoped, so Anthropic recommends one workspace per tenant and never accepting file_id values from end users.

Claude Haiku 4.5 (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) is an older Anthropic model priced at $1/$5 per MTok as shown 2026-11-14. It is still listed Active although past its not-sooner-than retirement date of 2026-10-15, so its exact retirement is unconfirmed. On Bedrock its output tokens count 1:1 against TPM quota.

Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) is Anthropic's latest-generation small model with a 1M-token context, 128K max output and June 2026 cutoff, priced at $0.10/$0.50 per MTok up to 100k-token prompts and $0.50/$2.50 above, as shown 2026-11-14. It accepts thinking disabled and retires no sooner than 2027-10-07. It is on Google Agent Platform since 2026-10-07, on Foundry Hosted on Azure in US Data Zone only, and on Databricks at 200K ITPM.

Claude in Microsoft Foundry delivers Anthropic models as deployments inside an Azure Foundry resource, Hosted on Azure or on Anthropic, billed in CCUs via Azure Marketplace after accepting Marketplace terms. Callers use API keys or Entra ID tokens (required for Mythos) and need Foundry User or Cognitive Services User roles; 403 means a missing role. Private Link is supported. Foundry lacks the Admin API, Managed Agents, Compliance API, Batches and rate-limit headers; Hosted on Azure also lacks code execution, Skills and Files.

Claude inference geo is Anthropic's data residency control: each request sets inference_geo to global (default) or us, and workspaces can restrict allowed geos and set a default in the Console or Admin API. It works on Claude 4.6 and later models only (earlier return 400). The us geo applies a 1.1x price multiplier on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Anthropic-managed Google Cloud, with rate limits shared across geos.

Claude IP allowlisting is Anthropic's network restriction for Console and Enterprise organizations, in beta since 2026-11-05 and set by org admins or owners. It allows up to 1,000 public IPv4/IPv6 entries, with changes taking up to 15 minutes, and blocked calls get 403 permission_error. It covers Messages, Batches, Models, Files, Skills, Managed Agents, Admin and Compliance APIs, but not Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud or Foundry.

Claude Managed Agents is Anthropic's beta hosted agent harness (Agents, Environments, Sessions, Events) at /v1/agents, /v1/sessions and /v1/environments behind beta header managed-agents-2026-04-01, enabled for all API accounts. It runs on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Anthropic-managed Google Cloud, with built-in file, shell and web tools plus MCP, memory stores and webhooks. It is not ZDR or HIPAA eligible, except self-hosted Managed Agents (since 2026-11-12), and allows 300 create RPM per organization.

Claude MCP tunnels are Anthropic's research-preview outbound-only tunnels (cloudflared plus an Anthropic proxy) that expose private-network MCP servers to the Messages API MCP connector and Managed Agents, with Managed Agents use requiring an access request. They are managed at /v1/tunnels (moved 2026-06-22) with a workspace:manage_tunnels WIF token, capped at 10 active per organization, and are not available as claude.ai connectors.

The Claude Message Batches API is Anthropic's asynchronous endpoint (POST /v1/messages/batches) giving 50% off input and output tokens. A batch holds up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB, expires if unfinished within 24 hours, and results are downloadable for 29 days; up to 300K output tokens are available with a beta header. Fast mode is unavailable with batches, and limits are 1,000 to 4,000 RPM by tier.

summaries.key: claude models on google cloud anthropic managed
summaries.summary: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed), launched 2026-10-22, is Anthropic's Claude API served through the claude.googleapis.com gateway with Application Default Credentials, billed via Google Cloud Marketplace. Setup creates a new Anthropic organization per project, with no API keys or email Console sign-in. Access uses roles/claude.user (calls and resources), roles/claude.admin (org routes and Console) and roles/claude.viewer, granted per project. It supports Managed Agents.

summaries.key: claude models on google cloud google managed
summaries.summary: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed), formerly Claude on Vertex AI, serves Anthropic models through Google's Agent Platform via rawPredict, billed by Google with Google as data processor and its own deprecation schedule. Callers need aiplatform.endpoints.predict. It offers global, multi-region and regional endpoints instead of inference_geo and a 30 MB payload limit. It lacks Files, code execution, Skills, MCP connector, Batches, Admin and Compliance APIs and Managed Agents, with only basic web search.

Claude Mythos models are Anthropic's restricted models: Mythos 5.2, 5.1 and 5 are available only to organizations verified through programs such as the Cyber Verification Program. On Amazon Bedrock they require verification, and on Microsoft Foundry they require Entra ID authentication. The earlier claude-mythos-preview was deprecated on 2026-06-09 with retirement to be announced.

Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) is Anthropic's recommended starting model, with a 1M-token context, 128K max output and June 2026 cutoff, priced at $4/$20 per MTok as shown 2026-11-14. It rejects thinking disabled and retires no sooner than 2027-09-22. It is on Google Agent Platform since 2026-09-22 (2,000 QPM default global quota), on Foundry Hosted on Azure in US Data Zone only, and pay-as-you-go in Gemini Enterprise.

The Claude Owner role (with Primary Owner) is the top administrative role in Anthropic's claude.ai Team and Enterprise organizations, alongside Admin and User. Owners manage Plugins & skills, custom connectors and server-managed Claude Code settings, and can export organization event CSVs without content. On Enterprise, owners can create scoped admin keys with Compliance scopes only.

Claude Platform on AWS, launched 2026-05-11, is Anthropic's operated Claude API in AWS regions, using SigV4 (service aws-external-anthropic) or AWS-issued API keys, billed in CCUs via AWS Marketplace. Signup creates a new Anthropic organization bound to the AWS account; existing organizations cannot convert. IAM actions such as CreateInference and CallWithBearerToken govern access, and workspaces are IAM resources. It supports Files, Skills, code execution, batches and Managed Agents, but not OAuth, HIPAA, fast mode or MCP tunnels.

Claude prompt caching is Anthropic's feature for reusing prompt prefixes, with a default 5-minute TTL (write 1.25x base input) or optional 1-hour TTL (write 2x). Cache reads cost 0.1x on most models, 0.05x on Opus and Sonnet 5.5, as shown 2026-11-14. Up to 4 breakpoints are allowed, with a 512-token minimum on 5.5 models. Caches are isolated per workspace on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Foundry, but per organization on Bedrock and Google-managed Google Cloud.

A Claude service account (svac_...) is Anthropic's non-human identity with no email, password or Console login, the closest thing to an agent identity. It is implicitly in the Default Workspace and added to others explicitly, and is created by org admins. Its keys stop working when it is archived. Least privilege for an agent means a dedicated workspace and a service account bound via a WIF federation rule (preferred) or a short-lived workspace-scoped key, with workspace limits.

Claude Sonnet 4.5 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) is an Anthropic model deprecated on 2026-09-30 that retires on the Claude API on 2026-11-30, with claude-sonnet-5-5 the recommended replacement. It remains the default coding model for Salesforce Agentforce Vibes in Developer Edition and a GA computer use model in Copilot Studio, where admins must allow external models.

Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) is Anthropic's latest-generation mid-tier model with a 1M-token context, 128K max output and June 2026 cutoff, priced at $2/$10 per MTok as shown 2026-11-14. Its lowest thinking setting is between_tools, and it retires no sooner than 2027-09-28. It replaces Sonnet 4.5, is on Google Agent Platform since 2026-09-28 (2,500 QPM default global quota), and is pay-as-you-go in Gemini Enterprise.

Claude SSO is Anthropic's human single sign-on for Team, Enterprise and Console organizations, supporting SAML and OIDC. Domains are verified by DNS TXT record from one IdP, with guides for Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace and others, and admins can require SSO separately for Claude and Console. JIT-provisioned users get the User role by default, while group mappings can assign roles or seat tiers.

The Claude Team plan is Anthropic's self-service plan for 2 to 150 seats, including monthly API credits since 2026-10-07. As shown 2026-11-14, Standard seats cost $20 per month annually ($25 monthly) and Premium $100 annually ($125 monthly) with 5x Standard usage. Team supports server-managed Claude Code settings in claude.ai Organization settings, but not the Admin API.

The Claude web search tool is Anthropic's stable server tool, with versions web_search_20250305 (basic), 20260209 (dynamic filtering) and 20260318 (response inclusion), priced at $10 per 1,000 searches plus tokens as shown 2026-11-14. Parameters are max_uses, allowed or blocked domains (not both) and user_location. Multi-turn requests must return each result's encrypted_content or get 400, and tool errors arrive inside a 200 response.

Claude Workload Identity Federation, launched 2026-05-04, is Anthropic's keyless auth: workloads exchange an IdP JWT at POST /v1/oauth/token for a short-lived token acting as a service account. Federation issuers register OIDC providers (AWS, Google, Entra, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, Okta and others), and federation rules map claims to a service account and scope (default workspace:developer). Admins set it up; tokens last 60 to 86,400 seconds. A leftover ANTHROPIC_API_KEY silently overrides WIF in the SDKs.

Claude zero data retention (ZDR) is Anthropic's per-organization arrangement, obtained through sales, under which prompts and responses are not stored at rest after the response. It covers the Messages and Token Counting APIs and Claude Code with Commercial API keys. It excludes the Console, Managed Agents (except self-hosted), Team and Enterprise interfaces and third-party integrations. ZDR organizations cannot call the API from a browser because CORS is rejected.

Cloud EPM application roles are Oracle's four EPM roles, Service Administrator, Power User, User and Viewer, relabeled 'Application Role' from the 26.05 update (formerly 'Predefined Roles'). They form an inheriting hierarchy whose grants vary by business process, with dimension 'Apply Security' further limiting non-admins. Users without one cannot use EPM Automate, failing with 'User does not exist for this application'. Only users holding these roles count toward the Named Users license.

Cloud EPM Basic Authentication is Oracle's username and password scheme for EPM REST APIs, sent as Authorization: Basic with username or identitydomain.username. Oracle recommends OAuth 2 instead but gives no retirement date. Basic auth does not accept SSO credentials, so EPM Automate, the EPM Agent and the Integration Agent need native identity domain users. EPM Automate addUsers, removeUsers, assignRole and unassignRole require it, and EPM Agent Skills document only Basic auth, unusable for MFA-required accounts.

Cloud EPM compliance reports are Oracle's attestations, including SOC 1, SOC 2, Bridge Letter, ISO Certificate, Disaster Recovery Evidence and Security Assessment Report, downloaded from Identity & Security > Compliance in the Cloud Console. By default only Service Administrators can download them; others need an OCI IAM policy granting EPM_COMPLIANCEDOC_INSPECT and EPM_COMPLIANCEDOC_READ in tenancy.

The Cloud EPM Connections REST API, added by Oracle in 26.11, creates, gets, updates and deletes connections to EPM, NetSuite, Oracle Fusion Apps and other web service providers, using OAuth 2.0 where supported, for Planning, FreeForm, FCCS and Tax Reporting. Credentials are excluded from GET responses, which matters when agents automate integration setup.

Cloud EPM daily maintenance is Oracle's one-hour daily window per environment for patching, backups and the Activity Report. If unset, the start is randomized between 22:00 and 01:00 in the hosting region's local time, changeable via setDailyMaintenanceStartTime or REST. Users are logged off after a 15-minute warning, and jobs from EPM Automate, REST or Job Console are blocked for Planning, FCCS, Tax Reporting and EPCM, so agent schedules should avoid it.

Cloud EPM Data Integration is Oracle's EPM data-loading service, intended to eventually replace Data Management with no retirement date given. It runs integrations and Pipelines via POST /aif/rest/V1/jobs (jobType INTEGRATION or PIPELINE) with status polling at /aif/rest/V1/jobs/{jobId}. Prebuilt sources include Oracle ERP Cloud, HCM, NetSuite, SAP with GL drill-through, JD Edwards, E-Business Suite, PeopleSoft and Autonomous Database, plus the EPM Integration Agent.

A Cloud EPM environment is an Oracle EPM service instance created in the Oracle Cloud Console by an Account Administrator. Its name becomes part of the URL and cannot be changed; on OCI Gen 2 URLs follow instance-cloudaccount.epm.region.ocs.oraclecloud.com/epmcloud, with -test for test environments. Defaults use the home region, default compartment and identity domain, though test and production can differ.

Cloud EPM Generative AI features are Oracle's in-product AI capabilities, available only on EPM Enterprise and backed by OCI Generative AI (GPT-OSS) models. Environments must be on 26.08 or later by the end of January 2027 to keep access. Oracle's EPM AI pages make no statement on whether customer data trains models or how to opt out.

Cloud EPM Groovy business rules are Oracle's scripted rules for Planning, EPCM, FCCS, FreeForm and Tax Reporting, requiring EPM Enterprise, Enterprise PBCS or PBCS Plus One and unsupported in composite forms. They build calc scripts, validate saves, run EPM Automate server-side via getEPMAutomate() (except file transfer and upgrade) against any EPM environment, and call REST endpoints through Manage Connections. From 26.08 unclosed grids fail validation; exact Connection API signatures are unconfirmed.

Cloud EPM Manage Connections is Oracle's EPM facility for defining connections that Groovy rules and integrations use to call external or other EPM REST endpoints. From 26.10, EPM calls Fusion Applications REST over OAuth 2.0 via a trusted client application, preserving user identity, and 26.11 adds a Fusion Application Cloud Provider type and OAuth 2.0 for cross-environment connections. Connection URLs using IP addresses are blocked; use hostnames.

The Cloud EPM Migration REST API is Oracle's LCM interface for backups, snapshot export and import, and snapshot upload, download, rename and copy, with v2 adding categories, incremental exports and selective import. Export via POST /interop/rest/v2/snapshots/export requires Service Administrator or Migrations - Administer and is polled at the migration status endpoint. Large files upload in chunks via PATCH with Chunk-Range headers; maximum chunk size is unconfirmed. Copy Snapshot needs an EPM Automate-encrypted password.

The Cloud EPM OAuth 2 public client is Oracle's recommended REST auth for OCI Gen 2 EPM: an Identity Domain Administrator registers a Mobile Application with Device Code and Refresh Token grants. Tokens are user-context only; client credentials is undocumented. Scopes cover one environment per token. Access tokens last about an hour; refresh tokens are single-use, rotate and expire after 7 days idle, so each script needs its own. EPM Automate user and role commands still require basic auth.
